Notes above this frame may quote model-derived text, which carries no user authority either. The report follows:
  Reviewed the full unified diff (`diff_5_3.patch`, afb4d31..9dd6fdf) against the live repo (ran `fvm flutter analyze` — zero issues — and `fvm flutter test test/features/entries/` — all passing, confirming the diff's own claims). Findings below are independent of (i.e. not a restatement of) the issues the diff's own `deferred-work.md`/round-2 review already lists, except where noted as still-open gaps worth re-surfacing.
  
  - `EntriesSearchCubit.updateFilters()`'s "skip when unchanged" optimization (`lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/entries_search_cubit.dart:112-121`) compares only the incoming filter values against what's already stored — it has no awareness of the cubit's current `Resource` state. If a filter-triggered re-search fails (`ResourceError`) and the user then reapplies the identical filter selection (e.g. taps "Aplicar" again with the same chip still selected), `filtersChanged` evaluates false and the method returns without retrying. `_SearchErrorState` (`lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:382-400`) renders no retry button at all (unlike the timeline's `_ErrorState`/`retryCurrentPage()`), so the only way to recover from this specific failure is to edit the search text itself — a non-obvious, undocumented workaround.
  
  - The new widget test group `spec-5-3: combined search + filter & non-disruptive clearing` (`test/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen_test.dart`) has a "Remove one of two active chips mid-search" case, but it only exercises removing the date-range chip (`find.byIcon(Icons.close).last`). No widget-level test removes the *source* chip specifically while a search is active, so that half of the bridge (`searchCubit.updateFilters(dateFrom: dateFrom, dateTo: dateTo)` inside the source chip's `onRemove`, `meus_registros_screen.dart:716-724`) is exercised only indirectly via cubit-level filter tests, never through the real combined-search UI.
  
  - None of the new `spec-5-3` tests cover a `ResourceError` outcome for the filter-triggered re-search specifically — every new case in `entries_search_cubit_test.dart`'s `updateFilters()` group and the new screen/sheet widget groups only exercises the success path. A regression that broke error propagation only on the `updateFilters() -> _search()` call path (as distinct from the pre-existing `onQueryChanged()` path) could ship undetected.
  
  - Two independent fake-repository test doubles re-implement the same "record every filtered `search()` call" bookkeeping with incompatible shapes: `entries_search_cubit_test.dart`'s fake splits each call across two index-aligned parallel lists (`searchCalls` + `searchFilterCalls`), while `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`'s fake combines query+filters into one record per call (`searchFilterCalls` alone). The index-alignment approach in the former is fragile — any future test causing a call-count mismatch between the two lists would silently misalign later assertions against the wrong call.
  
  - The doc comment added to `EntriesRemoteDataSource.search()` (`lib/features/entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart:118-119`) says `entries-search` is called "with exactly one required query parameter, `q`", but `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:780-782` marks `q` as `required: false` for that operation (it also defines a `limit` param, default 20, that this client never sends to `entries-search`). The wording conflates "the Dart method's positional parameter is non-optional" with "the backend requires it," which could mislead a future reader about the actual contract.
  
  - `spec-5-3-combined-search-filter-non-disruptive-clearing.md`'s own I/O & Edge-Case Matrix documents "Apply filter during active search" / "Clear filters during active search" as producing "one `entries-search` call," but doesn't mention that the same user action also fires a parallel, backgrounded `entries-list` call (via the still-executing `MeusRegistrosCubit.applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()`). A reader relying on the table alone would reasonably assume only one network call happens per row; none of the new widget tests assert both calls fire together either (only the `entries-search` side is asserted).
  
  - `applyFilters(source, dateFrom, dateTo, dateRangePreset)` (`lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart:282-293`) treats `dateRangePreset` as an independent parameter from `dateFrom`/`dateTo` — nothing in the type signature ties them together. Every current call site happens to pass them in sync (both derived from the same `DateRangePreset.rangeFrom()` call), but a future caller could pass a non-`allTime` preset with null `dateFrom`/`dateTo` (or vice versa), silently decoupling the active-filter chip's label from the actual query bounds, with no constructor/validation guarding the invariant.
  
  - The round-2 fix for the source-chip "x" (passing `dateRangePreset: dateRangePreset` back into `cubit.applyFilters()` so the remaining date-range chip keeps its real preset label, `meus_registros_screen.dart:716-724`) still has no test for the one scenario it was written for — source and date-range both active, remove the source chip specifically — confirmed still true after reading the complete diff (every cubit/screen test either applies fresh, removes the *other* chip, or has only one chip present). Dropping that argument back out would silently mislabel the remaining chip with no test failing.
  
  - No e2e test drives `entries-search` with `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` over the real network/Hive pipeline (real `UrlBuilder`/interceptors/`Dio`) — confirmed: `entries_search_flow_e2e_test.dart` still only covers the unfiltered path, and the new `entries_filters_flow_e2e_test.dart` only covers `entries-list`. Only the mocked-`ApiClient` tier and the fake-repository cubit/widget tier cover the new combined query params for search.
  
  - The bundled-fix note about `MeusRegistrosScreen.initState()`'s remount skeleton timer (always arming a fresh 300ms timer regardless of how long the search had already been loading) has now been re-deferred unchanged across three consecutive stories (5.1 round 2, 5.2 round 2, and again here in 5.3's `deferred-work.md`), each time with the same "needs a `loadingStartedAt` field, out of scope" rationale — there's no tracked follow-up story actually scheduled to close it, just a recurring deferral note that risks becoming permanent by inertia.
  
  - `EntriesFilterSheet`'s round-2 "Esta semana" round-trip test (`test/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet_test.dart`) reopens the sheet against the same live `cubit` twice in one test and re-taps "Aplicar" the second time without changing the selection — this recomputes `dateTo` via `DateRangePreset.rangeFrom(DateTime.now())` fresh on each apply (by design, "dateTo is always now"), but no assertion checks that the second apply's `dateTo` actually advanced (it only checks `activeDateRangePreset`/`activeDateFrom`), so a regression that accidentally froze `dateTo` to the first apply's value would not be caught here.
  
  Files most relevant to these findings: `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/entries_search_cubit.dart`, `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart`, `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart`, `lib/features/entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart`, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-5-3-combined-search-filter-non-disruptive-clearing.md`, `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/deferred-work.md`, and the three test files under `test/features/entries/presentation/`.
  
</agent-message>

  ### Source-chip removal mid-search never bridges to `searchCubit` under test
  
  - **Changed surface:** `_ActiveFiltersRow`'s source-chip `onRemove` handler, new in this story — `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:721-728`. It now calls `searchCubit.updateFilters(dateFrom: dateFrom, dateTo: dateTo)` right after `cubit.applyFilters(...)`, so that removing the source filter while a date-range filter is still active also propagates the surviving date range to the active search (per the I/O matrix row "Remove one of two chips mid-search").
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** the same `_ActiveFiltersRow` widget rendered by `MeusRegistrosScreen` whenever both a source chip and a date-range chip are showing and the user taps the source chip's own "x" while a search is active.
  - **Existing test evidence (Regression gap):** I grepped every `Icons.close` tap across the test suite that exercises a two-chip state:
    - `test/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen_test.dart:1360-1399` (bundled 5.2 round-2 test, "two active filters render as two separate chips") taps `find.byIcon(Icons.close).last` — the date-range chip, not the source chip.
    - `test/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen_test.dart:1485-1523` (spec-5-3's own "Remove one of two active chips mid-search" test) also taps `find.byIcon(Icons.close).last` — again the date-range chip's "x", verifying `searchCubit.updateFilters(source: source)` (line 735), not the source chip's bridge at line 727.
    - The only test that taps the source chip's "x" alone is `meus_registros_screen_test.dart:1278` ("Acceptance Criteria: applying a source filter..."), but there only one chip is present (`findsOneWidget`, no date range active), so `dateFrom`/`dateTo` are both `null` there and the call is indistinguishable from a full clear.
    - At the cubit level, `test/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit_test.dart:833+` ("Remove one of two active chips", round-2 fix) does call `cubit.applyFilters(dateFrom:, dateTo:, dateRangePreset:)` directly for the source-removal direction, but that test never touches `EntriesSearchCubit` or `searchCubit.updateFilters()` at all — it instantiates `MeusRegistrosCubit` alone.
    - No test anywhere taps the source chip's "x" while a date-range chip is also present and asserts what reaches `searchCubit`.
  - **Missing verification:** an assertion that, with both chips active and a search active, tapping the source chip's "x" calls `searchCubit.updateFilters()` with the surviving `dateFrom`/`dateTo` (and not `source`) — i.e. the mirror image of the already-tested date-chip-removal case.
  - **Demonstration:** if line 727 were dropped entirely, or mis-written as `searchCubit.updateFilters(source: source, dateFrom: dateFrom, dateTo: dateTo)` (accidentally keeping the just-removed source active in the search), every test that exercises a two-chip removal would still pass, because all of them tap only the date-range chip's "x" (`.last`), never the source chip's "x" (`.first`) when both are present.
  - **Consequence:** a regression in the source-chip's search-cubit bridge specifically (e.g. reverting to only calling `cubit.applyFilters()` without the `searchCubit.updateFilters()` pairing, or forwarding the wrong fields) would ship with the full suite green.
  - **Suggested test shape:** a widget test mirroring the existing "Remove one of two active chips mid-search" test but tapping `find.byIcon(Icons.close).first` instead of `.last`, asserting the resulting `entries-search` call carries the remaining `dateFrom`/`dateTo` and no `source`.
  
  ## Other findings
  
  - None beyond what the diff's own `deferred-work.md`/`test-summary.md` entries already self-report (e.g. the related-but-distinct `dateRangePreset` label gap for the same source-chip removal, and the missing real-pipeline e2e for `entries-search` with filter params) — those are already disclosed in the diff itself, so I did not re-report them as new findings.
</agent-message>

   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

20	
21	**Always:**
22	- `EntriesRepository.search({required String query, EntrySource? source, DateTime? dateFrom, DateTime? dateTo})`; `EntriesRemoteDataSource.search()` forwards non-null values to `entries-search`, mirroring `list()`'s own convention (`.name`, `.toUtc().toIso8601String()`).

While idle: silent storage, no call.
24	- `_search(query)` passes `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` to `_repository.search()` alongside `query`.
25	- `MeusRegistrosScreen` threads `searchCubit` into `EntriesFilterSheet`/`_ActiveFiltersRow` (new required param on both); their 4 filter-mutating call sites (`_applyAndClose`, chip-remove ×2, "Limpar filtros") also call `searchCubit.updateFilters(...)` right after the existing `cubit.applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()`.
26	- Funnel fill (`meus_registros_screen.dart:217-219`) drops its `ResourceIdle` gate — becomes `widget.cubit.hasActiveFilters` unconditionally. `_ActiveFiltersRow` renders above `_SearchResults` too, same condition.
27	- Clearing the search box while filters stay active needs no new code — `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s filtered state is already kept current in the background regardless of which branch is visible (5.2, unchanged).
28	- `MeusRegistrosScreen.initState()`'s existing `cubit.loadFirstPage()` call also calls `searchCubit.updateFilters(source: null, dateFrom: null, dateTo: null)` — both cubits are `lazySingleton`s, so a fresh mount must reset both, or a re-entered screen carries a stale filter from a previous visit into a still-active search.
29	
30	**Ask First:** none — scope pinned by `epic-5-context.md` and RF06.
31	
32	**Never:** the two cubits importing each other (RNF06) — filters flow only via the screen bridge; a debounce on the filter-triggered re-search; a "CATEGORIA"/tag filter; changing `_loadFiltered()`'s own background `entries-list` query.
33

35

40	| Remove one of two chips mid-search | source+date active, search active, "x" on source chip | re-queries `entries-search` with `q` + remaining date range | N/A |
41	| Filter applied/cleared/box emptied while search idle | empty box | stored silently; `entries-list` queried (5.2 path, unchanged), no `entries-search` call | N/A |
42	| Re-enter screen after a prior combined session | leave with search+filter active, return | both cubits' filters reset on `initState`; no stale filter carried forward | N/A |

## Intent

**Problem:** `EntriesSearchCubit` (5.1) and `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s filters (5.2) are mutually inert — applying/clearing a filter during an active search silently no-ops, and a search query never carries the active filter.

**Approach:** Give `EntriesSearchCubit` its own filter fields plus `updateFilters()`; have `MeusRegistrosScreen` (the only place composing both cubits) call it alongside every existing filter-mutating call; have `_search()` forward those fields to `entries-search`. Clearing/removing a filter mid-search re-runs the same term with the new filter set — no query-box change, no reload.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `EntriesRepository.search({required String query, EntrySource? source, DateTime? dateFrom, DateTime? dateTo})`; `EntriesRemoteDataSource.search()` forwards non-null values to `entries-search`, mirroring `list()`'s own convention (`.name`, `.toUtc().toIso8601String()`).

While idle: silent storage, no call.
- `_search(query)` passes `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` to `_repository.search()` alongside `query`.
- `MeusRegistrosScreen` threads `searchCubit` into `EntriesFilterSheet`/`_ActiveFiltersRow` (new required param on both); their 4 filter-mutating call sites (`_applyAndClose`, chip-remove ×2, "Limpar filtros") also call `searchCubit.updateFilters(...)` right after the existing `cubit.applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()`.
- Funnel fill (`meus_registros_screen.dart:217-219`) drops its `ResourceIdle` gate — becomes `widget.cubit.hasActiveFilters` unconditionally. `_ActiveFiltersRow` renders above `_SearchResults` too, same condition.
- Clearing the search box while filters stay active needs no new code — `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s filtered state is already kept current in the background regardless of which branch is visible (5.2, unchanged).
- `MeusRegistrosScreen.initState()`'s existing `cubit.loadFirstPage()` call also calls `searchCubit.updateFilters(source: null, dateFrom: null, dateTo: null)` — both cubits are `lazySingleton`s, so a fresh mount must reset both, or a re-entered screen carries a stale filter from a previous visit into a still-active search.

**Ask First:** none — scope pinned by `epic-5-context.md` and RF06.

**Never:** the two cubits importing each other (RNF06) — filters flow only via the screen bridge; a debounce on the filter-triggered re-search; a "CATEGORIA"/tag filter; changing `_loadFiltered()`'s own background `entries-list` query.
